source_text: Πρὸς τούτοις δὲ θαυμάσαι ἄν τις, πόθεν ἐπῆλθε τοῖς μαθηταῖς αὐτοῦ, ὡς λέγουσιν οἱ κακολογοῦντες τὸν Ἰησοῦν, μὴ ἑωρακόσιν αὐτὸν ἀναστάντα ἀπὸ τῶν νεκρῶν μηδὲ πεισθεῖσιν ὅτι θειότερόν τι ἦν ἐκεῖνος, πρὸς τῷ μὴ φοβηθῆναι τὰ αὐτὰ τῷ διδασκάλῳ παθεῖν καὶ ὁμόσε χωρῆσαι τῷ κινδύνῳ καὶ καταλιπεῖν τὰς πατρίδας ὑπὲρ τοῦ διδάξαι κατὰ τὸ Ἰησοῦ βούλημα τὸν παραδοθέντα αὐτοῖς ὑπ᾿ αὐτοῦ λόγον. οἶμαι γὰρ ὅτι ὁ εὐγνωμόνως ἐξετάζων πράγματα οὐκ ἂν λέγοι τούτους ἑαυτοὺς παραδεδωκέναι περιστατικῷ βίῳ ἕνεκεν τῆς Ἰησοῦ διδασκαλίας χωρίς τινος μεγάλης πειθοῦς, ἣν ἐνεποίησεν αὐτοῖς διδάσκων οὐ μόνον διακεῖσθαι κατὰ τὰ μαθήματα αὐτοῦ ἀλλὰ καὶ ἄλλους διατιθέναι, καὶ διατιθέναι προὔπτου ὄντος ὡς πρὸς τὸν ἀνθρώπων βίον ὀλέθρου τῷ τολμῶντι πανταχοῦ καὶ πρὸς πάντας καινοτομεῖν καὶ μηδένα ἀνθρώπων, ἐμμένοντα τοῖς προτέροις δόγμασι καὶ ἔθεσι, φίλον ἑαυτῷ τηρεῖν. ἆρα γὰρ οὐχ ἑώρων οἱ τοῦ Ἰησοῦ μαθηταὶ, τολμῶντες οὐ μόνον Ἰουδαίοις ἐκ τῶν προφητικῶν λόγων παριστάνειν ὅτι οὗτος εἴη ὁ προφητευθεὶς, ἀλλὰ καὶ τοῖς λοιποῖς ἔθνεσιν ὅτι ὁ χθὲς καὶ πρώην σταυρωθεὶς ἑκὼν τοῦτον τὸν θάνατον ὑπὲρ τοῦ τῶν ἀνθρώπων γένους ἀνεδέξατο, ἀνάλογον τοῖς ἀποθανοῦσιν ὑπὲρ πατρίδων ἐπὶ τῷ σβέσαι λοιμικὰ κρατήσαντα καταστήματα ἢ ἀφορίας ἢ δυσπλοΐας; εἰκὸς γὰρ εἶναι ἐν τῇ φύσει τῶν πραγμάτων κατά τινας ἀποῤῥήτους καὶ δυσλήπτους τοῖς πολλοῖς λόγους φύσιν τοιαύτην, ὡς ἕνα δίκαιον ὑπὲρ τοῦ κοινοῦ ἀποθανόντα ἑκουσίως ἀποτροπιασμοὺς ἐμποιεῖν φαύλων δαιμονίων, ἐνεργούντων λοιμοὺς ἢ ἀφορίας ἢ δυσπλοΐας ἤ τι τῶν παραπλησίων. λεγέτωσαν οὖν οἱ βουλόμενοι ἀπιστεῖν τῷ Ἰησοῦν ὑπὲρ ἀνθρώπων ἀποτεθνηκέναι τρόπῳ σταυροῦ, πότερον οὐδὲ τὰς Ἑλληνικὰς παραδέξονται καὶ βαρβαρικὰς πολλὰς ἱστορίας περὶ τοῦ τινας ὑπὲρ τοῦ κοινοῦ τεθνηκέναι καθαιρετικῶς τῶν προκαταλαβόντων τὰς πόλεις καὶ τὰ ἔθνη κακῶν· ἢ ἐκεῖνα μὲν γεγένηται οὐδὲν δὲ πιθανὸν ἔχει ὁ νομιζόμενος ἄνθρωπος πρὸς τὸ ἀποθανεῖν ἐπὶ καθαιρέσει μεγάλου δαίμονος καὶ δαιμόνων ἄρχοντος, ὑποτάξαντος ὅλας τὰς ἐπὶ γῆν ἐληλυθυίας ἀνθρώπων ψυχάς; ὁρῶντες δὲ ταῦτα οἱ τοῦ Ἰησοῦ μαθηταὶ καὶ ἄλλα τούτων πλείονα, ἃ εἰκὸς αὐτοὺς ἐν ἀποῤῥήτῳ ἀπὸ τοῦ Ἰησοῦ μεμαθηκέναι, ἔτι δὲ καὶ δυνάμεώς τινος πληρωθέντες. ἐπεὶ ἔδωκεν αὐτοῖς μένος καὶ θάρσος οὐ ποιητική τις παρθένος ἀλλ᾿ ἡ ἀληθῶς φρόνησις καὶ σοφία τοῦ θεοῦ, (ἔσπευσαν,) ἵν᾿ ἔκδηλοι μετὰ πᾶσιν οὐ μόνοις Ἀργείοις γένοιντο ἀλλὰ καὶ πᾶσιν Ἕλλησιν ὁμοῦ καὶ βαρβάροις, καὶ κλέος ἐσθλὸν ἄροιντο.
pass_a_gloss: One would also marvel at from where it came to the disciples of Jesus, as those who speak evil of Jesus say, that they did not see him risen from the dead, nor were they persuaded that he was something divine, in addition to not being afraid of the same things that the teacher suffered, and to have gone to the same danger, and to have left their homelands for the sake of teaching according to Jesus' will the word delivered to them by him. For I think that one examining things with gratitude would not say that they gave themselves over to a circumstantial life on account of Jesus' teaching without some great persuasion, which he worked in them by teaching, not only to live according to his teachings, but also to set others in order, and to set in order, even though it is dangerous for one's life to innovate everywhere and in front of everyone, and not to keep as a friend anyone of the people who remain in the former doctrines and customs. Did the disciples of Jesus, then, not see that, daring not only to present to the Jews from the prophetic words that he was the one prophesied, but also to the other nations that the one crucified yesterday and the day before willingly accepted this death on behalf of the human race, similarly to those who die on behalf of their homelands in order to extinguish pestilential powers or difficulties or turmoil? For it is likely that in the nature of things, according to certain unspeakable and hard-to-believe words to the many, such a nature exists, that one righteous person, having died voluntarily on behalf of the common good, would drive away the frightful things of evil demons, which work pestilence or difficulties or turmoil or something similar. Let those who wish to disbelieve that Jesus died on behalf of humans in the manner of the cross say, then, whether they will not also accept the Greek and barbarian histories, many of which are about some people having died on behalf of the common good, abolishing the evils that had taken hold of the cities and nations. Or did those things happen, but the man thought to have died for the abolition of a great demon and the demons that rule, having subjected all the souls of humans that have come upon the earth, is not believable? But seeing these things and many more of them, which it is likely they learned from Jesus in secret, and also being filled with some power, since he gave them courage and confidence, not from some created virgin, but from the true wisdom and intelligence of God, they hastened to become manifest to all, not only to the Argives, but also to all the Greeks and barbarians, and to gain good fame.
pass_b_english: One might also wonder where the disciples of Jesus found the resolve that their critics claim they had, given that they never saw him risen from the dead and were never convinced he was divine. These same critics point out that the disciples showed no fear of suffering the same fate as their teacher; they embraced the same danger, left their homelands, and devoted themselves to teaching the message Jesus had entrusted to them, acting on his will. I suspect that anyone who examines the situation fairly would refuse to say these men surrendered themselves to such a precarious existence for the sake of Jesus' teaching unless a powerful conviction had taken hold of them. That conviction came through his instruction, which shaped them not only to live by his lessons themselves but to set others right as well—even though challenging every convention in public at every turn puts one's life at risk and wins no friends among those who cling to the old doctrines and customs.

Did the disciples not see, as they dared to show the Jews from the prophetic writings that this was the foretold one, and to proclaim to the nations that the man crucified just days before had willingly accepted death for the whole human race? Their claim parallels those who die for their countries to stop a plague, a famine, or a storm at sea. It is plausible that the nature of things operates on certain unspeakable and hard-to-grasp principles, so that one righteous person dying voluntarily for the common good can drive off the destructive work of evil demons—demons that bring pestilence, scarcity, shipwreck, or similar evils. So let those who refuse to believe that Jesus died for humanity on a cross answer this: will they also reject the many Greek and barbarian histories that tell of individuals who died for their people and thereby removed the evils gripping their cities and nations? Or do they admit those stories happened, yet insist it is incredible that a man thought to have died to overthrow a great demon and the ruling demons who had subjected every human soul on earth could be believable?

The disciples saw all this and more—things they likely learned from Jesus in private—and they were also filled with a power not of human origin. Since the true wisdom and intelligence of God, not some created virgin, gave them courage and confidence, they hurried to make their witness known to everyone—not only to the Argives, but to all Greeks and barbarians alike—and to win an honorable reputation.

review.notes: Pass A fails on several counts of accuracy and completeness compared to the Greek. 1. Inaccuracy: 'εὐγνωμόνως' is translated as 'with gratitude' in Pass A, whereas it means 'judiciously' or 'wisely' (the context is about a person examining things wisely/judiciously). 2. Inaccuracy: 'ἐνεποίησεν' is translated as 'worked in them' in Pass A, but the Greek 'ἐνεποίησεν αὐτοῖς' refers to the persuasion/conviction he worked in them, which Pass A handles poorly by saying 'which he worked in them by teaching... to live according to his teachings'. 3. Inaccuracy: 'παρίστανειν' is translated as 'present' in Pass A, but in the context of 'παριστάνειν ὅτι οὗτος εἴη ὁ προφητευθεὶς', it means 'to demonstrate' or 'to show/prove'. 4. Inaccuracy: 'δυσπλοΐας' is translated as 'turmoil' in Pass A, but the lemma/choice list identifies it as 'difficulties'. 5. Inaccuracy: 'ἀποῤῥήτῳ' is translated as 'in secret' in the lemma/choice list, but the Greek 'ἐν ἀποῤῥήτῳ' (in the unspeakable/unutterable) is rendered as 'in secret' in the choice list, which is a semantic shift from the Greek 'unspeakable/unutterable'. 6. Inaccuracy: 'παρθένος' is translated as 'created virgin' in Pass A, which is a significant mistranslation of 'ποιητική τις παρθένος' (some created/made virgin). Pass B is a much better rendering, but Pass A is the primary translation being checked for fidelity to the Greek and must pass.
reasons: Pass A translates 'εὐγνωμόνως' as 'with gratitude' instead of 'judiciously/wisely'; 'ἐνεποίησεν' is poorly rendered; 'παριστάνειν' as 'present' misses the sense of 'demonstrating/proving'; 'ἀποῤῥήτῳ' is translated as 'in secret' in the lemma list which contradicts the Greek 'unspeakable/unutterable' used in the text.
